title: The Lantern-Wright's Tally
author: Lissa Tal, lantern-wright
body:
# Lanterns made

*Scratched on cloudy horn.*

---

Four for the Gate. One for old Mor, who went in the water at Candle Night, as she wanted.

Four for the Gate. None for the water. A good month.

*This month:* Six, and all six burn down. Not guttering. Burning down, the flame hanging from the wick like a drop of water, and pointing at the channel.

*Under it:* My mother said a lantern that burns down is looking for its owner. I have not made any for the drowned this month. They are looking anyway.

title: A Carrier's Note
author: Doran ko-Oskel, lead-carrier
body:
# To whoever lights the pole

*Scratched on lead.*

---

We have carried lead past this pole for sixty years. There has never been a light on it.

This month there is a light on it every night we come down, the reedfolk kind, the kind they put on the water for their dead.

*Under it:* We are not dead. We have counted each other. If it is a courtesy, thank you. If it is a warning, we would like to know what for, and we would like to know before we cross.

title: The Byre Count
author: the Oskel of the flat
body:
# Beasts in the byre

*Cut into the doorpost, low to high.*

---

Twelve head, the year we came down. Twenty. Twenty-six, the best year. Twenty, the water at the door. Nine, the water in. None: we have gone up.

*Above them all, fresh:* Nine. The same nine. I know them by their names, and the names are cut here in my grandfather's knife-hand, and my grandfather has been in the Oskel's ground for thirty years.

title: The Hummock Lanterns
author: the lantern-keepers of Moreva
body:
# Lit for the ones not given back

*Indigo on reed-cloth.*

---

Sa'mor, the eel-man, the flood year. Lissa'oul, a child. Nauve Tal, who went out to look for Lissa'oul.

*Tal. We wait. The water gives back.*

*The newest, the indigo still wet:* A lantern for Issa Moul of Moreva. Issa Moul is at her door in Moreva this morning, mending nets. She lit it herself. She says it is to save time.

title: What the Family Said
author: as told to Nauve Oul of Moreva
body:
# From the beams

*Written down by a neighbour.*

---

We are not mad. We have been told. The water is coming back, as the grandmothers said. Not a flood. A turning. The tide that went out a thousand years ago is at the bottom of its going.

We are waiting where our house came down to meet it, so that it knows where to find us.

*Under it, in the neighbour's hand:* I asked who told them. They said: the Mere, at dawn, at the Stride's Foot bench. I have walked there. I sat. I have not come back as sure as they are. I have come back less sure than I was.

title: The Pushed
author: the Eelweir
body:
# Pushed in

*A line an autumn.*

---

A Tallyman's clerk, by Issa Tal, who was sorry. Issa Tal, by the same clerk, who was not.

*And so on, a line a year, both sides, for longer than the board.*

*This autumn:* Nobody. We stood on the weir, the two sides, and waited for somebody to do it, and nobody did, and the eels went through under our feet, and everybody went home dry.

*Under it:* It is the first year the agreement has not been kept. Nobody has read it. Nobody knows what happens now.

title: The Family's Mark
author: as copied by a neighbour at Isseva
body:
# The Mor'oul platform

*Indigo on reed-cloth.*

---

Mor'oul: the eel-pool family. Five on the platform: the grandmother, two sons, two children. All went to Isseva the year the stilts started going. All living.

*Under it:* Five lanterns on the stilts this month, one each. Tal. We do not light lanterns for the living. Somebody is lighting them early.

title: The Pole-Keeper's Knots
author: the reedfolk of the North Fen
body:
# Lit at dusk

*Knotted round the pole.*

---

Lit, and seen from the Drowned Road. Lit. Lit, and a heron on the pole in the morning.

*This month:* Lit, by nobody, and under the water beside the path, the light coming up green through the peat.

*Under it:* Tal. We wait. Whoever lit it is standing a stride off the safe way, in the water, holding it up. We have not gone to see who. We have left a second lantern on the pole, lit, in case they would like one they can see by.

title: The Cutters' Count
author: the peat-cutters of the Delta
body:
# Poles home

*Notched on a spade handle.*

---

Nine poles from the hags to the Light. Nine, the fog thick. Nine, the fog so thick we held each other's belts.

*Last week:* Ten. Ten, between the sixth and seventh, lit, with rags the colour of old indigo, the colour our grandmothers dyed.

*Under it:* We walked past it and did not look up. In the morning there were nine. Tal says wait. We are waiting. We are also going home by the causeway.

title: The Smoker's Takings
author: Mor Tal, eel-smoker
body:
# Sold at the hut

*Knots in a smoky cord, and what they mean.*

---

To a carter, six eels, a penny. To a reedwoman, six eels, a penny. One price. Tal.

*This month, at night:* To somebody I do not see, six eels, a penny left on the step. Old pennies, with the bell whole on them. The Vale has not struck those since the Toll cracked.

*Under it:* They are good pennies. I have kept them. I have kept smoking.

title: The Trader's Manifest
author: the master of the Sweet Tally
body:
# Cargo

*In a brass tube.*

---

Lime, forty sacks. Brass wire, three coils. A crate for the Traders' Post, not to be opened.

*Added, water-stained:* The tide is going out. We are staying with her. The crate has been opened. We did not open it.
